name: DOLLARFR
description: DOLLARFR converts a decimal dollar value into fractional notation, commonly used for bond prices quoted in 32nds or 64ths.
tldr: Converts a decimal dollar price into a fractional dollar price.

parameters.name: decimal_dollar
parameters.description: Decimal number to convert to a fraction.

parameters.name: fraction
parameters.description: Integer to use in the denominator of the fraction.

basicExample.explanation: 1.125 equals 1 and 2/16, so the result is 1.02.

howItWorks: DOLLARFR converts a decimal value to a number where the integer part is the whole dollar amount and the decimal part is the numerator over the specified fraction.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Result is not a true fraction but a number in fractional notation.
Use DOLLARDE to convert back to decimal.

commonErrors.fix: Use an integer for the fraction.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: DOLLARFR works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between DOLLARFR and DOLLARDE?
faq.answer: DOLLARFR converts decimal to fractional. DOLLARDE converts fractional to decimal.

faq.question: When is DOLLARFR used?
faq.answer: It is used to display bond prices in fractional notation.
